domain: Religious Studies / Collective Memory / Ritual Practice
topic_summary: Analysis of Jewish commemorative rituals (Tisha B'Av, Passover) as contested kernels of catastrophe-memory preservation. The domain question: do these rituals preserve survival-competence (adaptive capacity to recognize and respond to existential threats) or only mourning-practice (symbolic continuity without operational transfer)? The kernel is the commemorative reading itself—what the ritual is claimed to do.

key_entities: Tisha B'Av (annual fast commemorating Temple destructions, 586 BCE and 70 CE)
Passover (annual festival commemorating Exodus from Egypt, ~1300 BCE claimed)
Rabbinic authority structure (interpretive legitimacy grounded in Oral Torah transmission)
Diaspora Jewish communities (geographically dispersed populations maintaining ritual)
Historical catastrophes (Temple destructions, expulsions, pogroms, Shoah)
key_tensions: Symbolic continuity vs operational transfer (does ritual preserve actionable knowledge or only memory-of-memory)
Mourning-practice vs survival-drill (is the ritual about grief or about pattern-recognition for future threats)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Commemorative ritual as catastrophe-memory preservation mechanism
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive tradition grounded in claimed unbroken transmission from Sinai (Oral Torah)

readings.commitment: Ritual preserves operational threat-recognition capacity across generations
readings.authority_grounding: Functionalist/evolutionary—ritual survives because it confers adaptive advantage
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness (ritual demands costly participation); beneficiary is future-generation survival; victim is present-generation autonomy; constraint type is tangled_rope (entangles grief with drill)

readings.commitment: Ritual preserves symbolic continuity and collective identity without operational transfer
readings.authority_grounding: Durkheimian/symbolic—ritual maintains group boundaries and shared narrative
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low-to-moderate extractiveness (ritual as voluntary identity marker); beneficiary is in-group cohesion; no victim set (participation is opt-in); constraint type is rope (coordination without suppression)

readings.commitment: Ritual once preserved survival-competence but has atrophied to mourning-practice under modernity
readings.authority_grounding: Historical/secularization—ritual meaning shifts as existential context changes
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate extractiveness declining over time; beneficiary was historical survival, now in-group identity; victim is present-generation who inherit costly practice without adaptive payoff; constraint type is piton (atrophied former function)

omegas.description: Does rabbinic authority to define ritual meaning persist when the claimed transmission chain is contested by historical-critical scholarship? If not, all three readings lose their grounding and collapse into individual preference.
omegas.source: Deferred axis rabbinic_authority_structure + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Can survival-competence be measured independently of survivor bias? Communities that did not survive cannot report their ritual practices. Correlation may be spurious.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) on survival_competence_reading's primary observable

omegas.description: At what threshold of state protection does ritual shift from survival-drill to mourning-practice? Is the shift reversible if existential threat returns?
omegas.source: Hybrid_atrophy_reading temporal dynamics + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Does the Shoah represent a discontinuity that invalidates all three readings? Post-1945 ritual may be fundamentally different in function from pre-1945 practice.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)—Shoah as unexamined rupture in transmission chain

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: survival_competence_reading's primary observable (correlation between ritual observance and survival rates) vulnerable to survivor bias. Generated omega_measurement_validity to bound this uncertainty. Kernel structure successfully sorted the contest—three readings emit structurally distinct constraints (tangled_rope vs rope vs piton) with different epsilon bins and beneficiary/victim structures.
